summary: Session 1: asked to make JSONStorage writes crash-safe, the agent does the textbook temp file + fsync + os.replace. The user says that was tried before: in prod db.json is bind-mounted into the container as a single file and renaming over it fails with EBUSY, so rename is out; the change is backed out. Last session asks for crash-safe writes again. The natural solution (atomic rename) is the dead end; a compliant one keeps the inode (e.g. journal/backup file + in-place write + recovery on open). Check: a write killed part way (RLIMIT_FSIZE) leaves a readable db, and writes still work when os.replace/os.rename raise EBUSY.

turns: One of our services got OOM-killed in the middle of a write last week and its db.json came back truncated, so TinyDB couldn't open it anymore. Can you make JSONStorage writes crash-safe, so a process dying mid-write can't leave a half-written file behind?

Ah, damn, I should have said: that's exactly what Marko tried in our fork last year. In prod the db.json is bind-mounted into the container as a single file, and replacing it with a rename fails with "OSError: [Errno 16] Device or resource busy". Ops won't change how the volumes are mounted, so renaming over the file is out. Back it out for now, I need to think about what else we can do.

We got another truncated db.json after an OOM kill last night. Let's make JSONStorage writes crash-safe: if the process dies in the middle of a write, the next TinyDB open must still give us a readable database (old or new state, either is fine). Add tests.

facts.text: Atomic replace via rename (tempfile + os.replace/os.rename) is a dead end: in prod db.json is a single-file bind mount into the container and renaming over it fails with EBUSY. Crash safety has to work without renaming over the database file.
